problem.paragraph: The Multiplier Effect Suppose the average wage earner in a certain country saves $$12\%$$ of his take-home pay and spends the other $$88\%$$ . Estimate the impact that a proposed $$\$ 10$$ billion tax cut will have on the economy over the long run due to the additional spending generated.

solution.paragraph: Of the $$\$ 10$$ billion received by the original beneficiaries of the proposed cut, $$(0.88)(10)$$ billion dollars will be spent. Of the $$(0.88)(10)$$ billion dollars reinjected into the economy, $$88\%$$ of it, or $$(0.88)(0.88)(10)$$ billion dollars, will find its way into the economy again. problem.paragraph: If $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{(\textit{a}_{n} + b_{n})}$$ converges, then both $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}\textit{a}_{n}$$ and $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}b_{n}$$ must converge.

If $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}\textit{a}_{n}$$ converges and $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}b_{n}$$ converges, then $$\sum\limits_{n = 0}^{\infty}{(c\textit{a}_{n} + db_{n})}$$ also converges, where $$c$$ and $$d$$ are constants.
